chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Safwan, from Abi Basir, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:
If a man becomes certain that he omitted a rak'ah of the salat (prayer), and he has already performed two sajdahs while having omitted the ruku', he must restart the salat (prayer).

key_terms.اسْتَأْنَفَ: he recommenced or restarted from the beginning
key_terms.سَجْدَتَيْنِ: the two prostrations within a rak'ah

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone forgets the ruku' and remembers after performing the two sajdahs in salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning one who becomes certain that he omitted the ruku' in a rak'ah after already performing the two sajdahs. In such a case, the salat (prayer) must be recommenced, showing the essential status of the ruku' within the structure of prayer.
